title: SpaceX Could Announce a Deal for Tesla as Soon as December. Here's What It Would Do to SpaceX Stock.
detail:
SpaceX Could Announce a Deal for Tesla as Soon as December. Here's What It Would Do to SpaceX Stock.
Daniel Sparks, The Motley Fool
Fri, November 13, 2026 at 1:32 PM PST 5 min read
SPCX
TSLA
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) and Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) have moved on to haggling over price and control in their merger talks, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, Nov. 12. A deal could be announced as soon as December, the report said, but early 2027 is possible too. And it's shaping up as SpaceX taking over Tesla, with Tesla investors getting SpaceX shares. Neither company commented.

The sizes alone make this unusual. At roughly $140 a share as of this writing, SpaceX is worth about $1.9 trillion, and Tesla, near $397, is worth almost $1.6 trillion.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

So, what would a deal do to SpaceX stock? At these prices, it could nearly double SpaceX's share count and leave its shareholders owning a company whose sales come mainly from Tesla. I think the second part matters more than the first.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

The share count could nearly double

Buying Tesla at its market value, without a premium, takes around 11.2 billion new SpaceX shares. SpaceX had around 13.6 billion Class A and Class B shares outstanding as of Oct. 15, according to its quarterly filing, so the count could grow around 83%.

This leaves today's SpaceX shareholders with about 55% of the combined company. Tesla holders, of course, will probably want a premium. At a 25% premium, SpaceX's current owners wind up with slightly less than half.

"Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes," CEO Elon Musk said about a merger on SpaceX's Oct. 20 earnings call. He added shareholders have to back it.

On SpaceX's side, the filing says any deal requires approval from its special committee, board, and controlling shareholder.

What would SpaceX shareholders own?

SpaceX's third-quarter revenue climbed 161% year over year to $14.6 billion, but Tesla's was flat at $28.0 billion. Put those reports together, and Tesla makes up around 66% of the combined total. Tesla's automotive revenue alone is about 48%. And the AI business SpaceX calls superintelligence shrinks from around half of SpaceX's sales to about 18% of the combined figure.

On those numbers, combined revenue rose only about 27% year over year.

Profit points the other way. SpaceX's third-quarter operating income was $2.8 billion, up from a loss the year before, while Tesla's dropped 56% to $718 million. So Tesla brings around two-thirds of the sales but only about a fifth of the operating income. The combined operating margin is about 8%, versus about 19% for SpaceX alone.

title: Tesla and SpaceX Move Closer to a Deal. What Would Tesla Shareholders Get?
detail:
Tesla and SpaceX Move Closer to a Deal. What Would Tesla Shareholders Get?
Moz Farooque ACCA
Fri, November 13, 2026 at 11:31 AM PST 2 min read
TSLA
SPCX
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) and SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) are making progress in merger talks and could announce a deal as early as December, Bloomberg reported Thursday. The two companies have a combined market value of roughly $3.4 trillion. For Tesla shareholders, the figure that matters most is how many SpaceX shares they could receive for each Tesla share.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with SPCX.

Is SPCX fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Reuters put SpaceX's market capitalization at about $1.9 trillion and Tesla's at about $1.55 trillion. Those figures give a sense of the potential merger's scale. Negotiators are still working through ownership and governance, and Bloomberg reported that an announcement could slip into early 2027.

Elon Musk, who leads both companies, confirmed in October that each board had formed a special committee of independent directors to examine a combination. A merger would bring Tesla's electric vehicles, energy storage and robotics operations together with SpaceX's rocket launches and Starlink satellite internet business.

The companies already work together on Terafab, a chipmaking venture that Musk says could produce its first test chip around May or June 2027. The proposed merger also raises national security questions because SpaceX holds U.S. defense contracts and Tesla has significant manufacturing operations in China.

Investors Takeaway

Tesla's Dec. 3 annual meeting is an early opportunity for investors to hear management address the talks. The published agenda contains no merger vote.

If the companies announce an agreement, the share exchange ratio will determine the value offered to Tesla holders and their ownership of the combined business. Board composition and the independent committees' valuation rationale will help shareholders assess how the deal allocates value between the two companies. Any conditions tied to SpaceX's defense contracts could also affect the closing timeline or force changes to the deal's structure.

title: Texas AG-elect vows 'tremendous scrutiny' of SpaceX-Tesla merger
detail:
Texas AG-elect vows 'tremendous scrutiny' of SpaceX-Tesla merger
Mateo Rosiles, USA TODAY NETWORK
Fri, November 13, 2026 at 11:29 AM PST 1 min read
SPCX
TSLA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The incoming Texas attorney general is signaling that he will scrutinize the potential merger between Elon Musk's SpaceX and Tesla.

In a Nov. 12 interview with Bloomberg, Texas Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson said "any merger of companies of that consequence warrants tremendous scrutiny."

"I think he's received a great deal of deference due to his alignment with the Republican Party and the tons of money he spent for the Republican Party," Johnson said. "I have no qualms about examining his relationships to the state."

BOCA CHICA, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 29: A SpaceX facility is seen beyond a shore near the Starbase on September 29, 2026 in Boca Chica, Texas. The Brownsville City Commission has come to an agreement with SpaceX on two substantial water projects that seek to add approximately 18 million gallons of water per day for the region.

Johnson, set to replace Republican Ken Paxton as the state's chief legal officer in January, is one of several Democrats who won control of statewide offices from Republicans on Nov. 3 for the first time since the 1990s.

Johnson did not discuss the specifics of any SpaceX-Tesla combination with Bloomberg and said his transition team hasn't been in touch with Musk, adding that "if Elon wants to talk, we can talk."

SpaceX and Tesla didn't immediately respond to USA TODAY's requests for comment.

Tesla is headquartered in Austin, and SpaceX's headquarters is at Starbase, Texas, near Brownsville.

What we know about the rumored SpaceX-Tesla merger

SpaceX and Tesla could eventually merge, according to Barron's and Bloomberg, which reported in October that a combination of Musk's companies is "widely expected" by investors.

While the merger details have not been made public, Bloomberg reported in November that the deal could be announced as soon as December.

title: Trader Loses $200K, Quits For 3 Years, Then Returns To Win It Back And Loses Another $100K. Says, ‘The FOMO Was Unbearable’

Trader Loses $200K, Quits For 3 Years, Then Returns To Win It Back And Loses Another $100K. Says, ‘The FOMO Was Unbearable’

A trader walked away after losing more than $200,000 on options. They spent three years watching tech stocks climb before they started trading again, hoping to win back what they lost. Instead, they ended up down another $100,000.

"The FOMO was unbearable," they wrote on Reddit.

They Thought Tesla Would Bounce Back

The poster opened a trading account because of the hype around GameStop (NYSE:GME). One of their early bets was on Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA). They bought call options and were up $80,000 at one point. "Thought I was a god at trading," they wrote.

That gain disappeared when Tesla's stock fell. The poster held on because they thought it would go back up. They eventually sold the options for half of what they paid.

They kept trading, betting on how stocks would move after earnings reports, Fed meetings, and inflation updates.

Some of the options they bought expired that same day. Within months of discovering options, they said, they'd lost more than $200,000 and wiped out their savings. They couldn't bring themselves to look at the account and stopped trading for three years.

They Gave The Same Bet One More Shot

The poster read about SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) on Reddit and bought put options, betting the stock would fall once early investors could sell their shares. Instead, it went from $130 to $150, and they kept buying puts as the price rose.

The bets cost them another $100,000. When SpaceX hit $170, they used the last of their savings to buy more put options. They made some money back, then lost part of it on a separate trade in Nasdaq-100 options. They used what was left in the account to buy SpaceX puts again. That trade paid off.

title: Elon Musk's SpaceX–Tesla Merger 'Almost Inconceivable' to Avoid, Biographer Says
detail:
Elon Musk's SpaceX–Tesla Merger 'Almost Inconceivable' to Avoid, Biographer Says
Daragh Thomas
Fri, November 13, 2026 at 11:45 AM PST 3 min read
SPCX
TSLA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Benzinga and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.

Elon Musk's biographer believes Tesla and SpaceX are destined to merge, arguing their increasingly intertwined technology ambitions make keeping them separate almost impossible.

"It's almost inconceivable that you would not merge these companies now," Walter Isaacson, a Tulane professor and Perella Weinberg advisory partner, told CNBC Friday.

Musk himself has been more cautious, warning last month that assuming a merger is certain "would be overstating it."

Isaacson's comments come as Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA) and Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) advance merger negotiations, with Bloomberg reporting Thursday that an announcement could come as early as December.

Bettors Doubt a December Deal

On Polymarket, the probability of an official merger announcement by Dec. 31 jumped from roughly 10% a week ago to 31% Friday.

Traders are more confident over a longer timeline, pricing an 81% chance by the end of 2027. The markets have attracted approximately $1.77 million in combined volume.

Isaacson expects more clarity at Tesla's Dec. 3 shareholder meeting.

"I definitely think this merger is going to play out," he said. "I don't know if it'll all be solved by then, but it's something that'll be discussed."

'It Makes No Sense Otherwise'

Isaacson's confidence comes down to Terafab, the enormous semiconductor manufacturing project Tesla and SpaceX are developing together.

"They're interconnected in doing it," he said. "I think you have to have a merger, it makes no sense otherwise."

Tesla needs specialized chips for self-driving vehicles and Optimus robots, while SpaceX wants computing power for AI infrastructure and potential orbital data centers.

Isaacson also pointed to the problems facing Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA), saying the merger makes even more sense "in an era when Nvidia is having such problems."

Musk's companies remain major Nvidia customers, and Isaacson doesn't expect that relationship to end.

"I assume they'll still get those deliveries of chips, that's not going to stop," he said.

But he believes the AI5 and AI6 chips Tesla and SpaceX are designing together could provide an alternative supply within two or three years, including processors configured to work in space.

The $3.45 Trillion Question

There is one question Isaacson didn't answer.

CNBC's interviewer asked whether Tesla shareholders would receive a takeover premium or simply exchange their shares for SpaceX stock.

title: General Motors vs. Tesla: Which Is the Better Automotive Stock to Buy Going Into 2027?
detail:
General Motors vs. Tesla: Which Is the Better Automotive Stock to Buy Going Into 2027?
Robert Izquierdo, The Motley Fool
Fri, November 13, 2026 at 10:37 AM PST 5 min read
GM
TSLA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investors face a choice between a legacy giant and an electric pioneer in General Motors (NYSE:GM) and Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) as they compete for dominance in an evolving global market.

General Motors focuses on transitioning its massive manufacturing scale to electric models while maintaining strong internal combustion sales. Tesla continues to disrupt the market by integrating software, autonomous vehicle (AV) technology, and energy storage into its automotive ecosystem. Both companies offer distinct paths within the automotive industry for those interested in the future of transportation.

The case for General Motors

General Motors serves retail and fleet customers through well-known brands including Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC. The company operates over 4,500 authorized dealers in North America and secures battery raw materials through long-term offtake agreements. GM Financial supports these operations by providing automotive financing solutions to customers and dealers, while strategic joint ventures in China involve partners like SAIC.

In the trailing 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached $187.0 billion, a decrease of 0.3% from the prior year. Net income during this period was $3.9 billion. This performance follows a trend of varying net margins as the company balances legacy and new vehicle investments during its ongoing transition to electric power.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 2.1x, meaning total liabilities are more than double the company's shareholder equity. The current ratio of 1.2x indicates the company has approximately $1.20 in current assets for every dollar of short-term debt. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was $11.1 billion, representing the cash remaining after a company pays for capital expenditures like equipment and facilities.

The case for Tesla

Tesla manufactures electric vehicles and energy storage products, selling them directly through its own retail network rather than using traditional dealerships. Its factories have the capacity to produce more than a million vehicles annually across North America, Europe, and Asia. The company also operates a global Supercharger network for car charging that is increasingly open to non-Tesla vehicles to support broader electric vehicle adoption.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached $103.6 billion, which was year-over-year growth of 8.3%. Net income was $3.2 billion during this timeframe. This expansion comes as the company increases its manufacturing, assembly, and service operations globally while maintaining a net margin of 3.1%.

title: Tesla-SpaceX Merger Talks Progress. Gary Black Sees “Little Windfall” for Tesla Holders
detail:
Tesla-SpaceX Merger Talks Progress. Gary Black Sees “Little Windfall” for Tesla Holders
Gian Estrada
Fri, November 13, 2026 at 10:16 AM PST 4 min read
TSLA
SPCX
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Tesla-SpaceX Merger Talks Progress. Gary Black Sees "Little Windfall" for Tesla Holders ©U.S. Air Force photo by Justin R. Pacheco and kb group via Canva
Key Takeaways

Tesla and SpaceX could announce a merger as soon as December. Dan Ives puts the odds at 90% and says Tesla needs to be "north of 500."

Gary Black expects "little windfall" for Tesla holders, because the premium would arrive in SpaceX stock.

Tesla holders would own about half the combined company, so they'd pay about half of any premium themselves.

The best case for a deal is SpaceX's growth, and anyone can buy SpaceX shares today.

Tesla (TSLA:NASDAQ) and SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) are making progress in merger talks and could announce a deal as soon as December, Bloomberg reported on Nov. 12. It would be the largest merger ever.

Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives put the odds at 90% on CNBC's Closing Bell that day, adding that Tesla needs to be "north of 500" for it to happen.

Gary Black, managing partner of The Future Fund, still expects an all-stock deal "will result in little windfall for TSLA investors given the massive dilution of SPCX shares and the long expected lead time (12-18 months) between deal announcement and deal close."

The math backs him up.

Tesla Holders Would Pay Half Their Own Premium

SpaceX is worth about $1.9 trillion and Tesla about $1.55 trillion. Black's own guess is a 20% to 25% premium. At 20%, Tesla holders would get SpaceX shares worth about $1.86 trillion, or about half the combined company.

So they'd fund about half the premium themselves. If the market values the combined company at the sum of its parts, a 20% premium is worth about 10% to Tesla holders, before synergies.

Twelve to 18 Months Is a Long Time

A stock premium is only worth what the acquirer's shares fetch at closing. From SpaceX's pre-deal price, a 17% drop would wipe out a 20% premium.

Marvell's all-stock deal for Lumentum shows how fast that can happen, as Black pointed out. Marvell offered a 24% premium over Oct. 28 closes. By the Nov. 4 close, Marvell had fallen 36%, leaving the offer worth about $720 a share, 21% below Lumentum's pre-deal price.

SpaceX hasn't been steady either. It fell 12% from Oct. 21, the first trading day after Musk confirmed the talks, to Nov. 12, when it closed 31% below its June 16 record close. Walling off Tesla's China business from SpaceX's defense work could also slow things down.
